annotations.text:
P.A.T.R.O.L. — second pass

What changed: light paper instead of dark tactical, Instrument Serif + Sans instead of IBM Plex, rows instead of cards, and colour reduced to one job — urgency. No pills, no badges, no monospace, no jargon.

Body text went from 9–11 px to 14–16 px. That was the biggest usability problem in the first pass.

"Now / Soon / Can wait" replaces Red/Yellow/Green. Same S.T.A.R.T. protocol underneath — a frightened person should not have to learn triage vocabulary.

Six categories instead of eight; fire and building collapse move behind a link.

Real offline vector basemap — streets, blocks, park, river — drawn here as a stand-in for MapLibre + a bundled .pmtiles extract.

This is a change from the plan, which said hand-rolled SVG. Doing it properly costs about 3 hours: see my note in chat.

Cut hard: no packet terminal, no dBm labels, no hex, no counters. Everything technical now sits behind "Technical details".

What's left answers the only two questions a user has — am I connected, and is my report getting through.
